stories.headline: Anthropic Signs $35 Billion With Lambda, and Nvidia Is Chip Seller, Investor and Landlord at Once
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic's $35 billion Lambda deal puts Nvidia in three roles at once - chip supplier, equity investor and holder of the Texas data center lease - sharpening scrutiny of circular AI financing just as Anthropic heads toward an IPO.

pull_quote.text: We recognize the scale of this support, and we know some will call this circular financing. We see it differently.

data_points.label: New Anthropic commitments in a week
Base-term value of Nvidia's Beacon Point leases

stories.article_excerpt: On a flat stretch of Nueces County, Texas, where a bitcoin miner once planned to hum through the night, Anthropic has bought six years of compute.

stories.headline: Huawei Says Its AI Chip Revenue Will Hit $12 Billion. Its Profit Fell 36% Getting There.
stories.key_takeaway: Huawei's AI chip business is booming on DeepSeek-driven domestic demand, but the R&D and input costs of building a China-only AI stack cut first-half profit by 36%.

pull_quote.text: Computing power is - and will continue to be - key to AI. This is especially true in China.
pull_quote.role: Deputy Chairman and Rotating Chairman, Huawei

stories.article_excerpt: Two numbers landed on Huawei's ledger this year, and they point in opposite directions.

stories.headline: Europe Just Spent 387.8 Million Euro on an AI Supercomputer, and Skipped Nvidia
stories.key_takeaway: EuroHPC's 387.8 million euro LUMI-AI contract hands AMD a second-generation win in Kajaani and makes a French state-owned Bull the builder of Europe's newest sovereign AI machine.

pull_quote.text: Europe's next wave of AI innovation will depend on infrastructure that is open, efficient and trusted.
pull_quote.role: SVP, Global Public Sector and Strategic Partnerships, AMD

data_points.label: AI capacity vs the existing LUMI system
Cores per 6th Gen AMD EPYC processor

stories.article_excerpt: The European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking signed a 387.8 million euro procurement contract on Aug. 31.

stories.headline: Clipto Raised $15 Million at a $250 Million Valuation. It Was Already Profitable.
stories.key_takeaway: Clipto raised $15M at a $250M valuation after already reaching $15M ARR and net-income profitability with just over 20 employees, betting that a local index of a user's own files becomes the memory layer AI agents plug into.

pull_quote.text: The real insight is that in this AI era, we don't have a content shortage. The opposite is true. We have too much content.

stories.article_excerpt: In 2006, a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon named Henry Kang built robots that recorded their surroundings.

stories.headline: A Robot Making Rounds on Hundreds of Nursing-Home Patients a Day Just Raised $14 Million
stories.key_takeaway: Norbert Health raised $14M to sell clinical skills as software that rides on other companies' robots, making it one of the few physical-AI startups with a year of paid production deployment rather than demos.

pull_quote.text: Robots that assist nurses can help reduce the burden, but only if they have clinical skills. Previous attempts put logistics robots on healthcare floors and never touched the core of a nurse's work.

stories.article_excerpt: The robot does not lift anyone. It does not change a dressing or push a med cart. What it does, several hundred times a day, is look.

stories.headline: Robotics Startups Have Already Beaten Last Year's Funding Total, With Months Left to Run
stories.key_takeaway: Robotics startups have raised $18.8B globally in 2026 - past both 2025's full-year $15B and the 2021 record of $14.1B - as venture capital rotates from application software into embodied AI, largely ahead of proven deployment revenue.

pull_quote.text: Solving intelligence for the physical world unlocks enormous commercial value and long-term strategic national importance.

data_points.label: China's share of global robotics investment

stories.article_excerpt: Sometime around the middle of this year, robotics stopped being a hardware bet and started being an AI bet.

stories.headline: Anthropic Cut Cache Reads 75% and Let Claude Look for Vulnerabilities Again
stories.key_takeaway: Anthropic left Fable 5.1's headline price untouched and instead cut cache reads 75% to $0.25 - a discount aimed squarely at long-running agents - while loosening cyber safeguards enough to let the model hunt vulnerabilities again, though not build exploits.

pull_quote.text: We're moving our Opus 5 traffic in Devin to Claude Fable 5.1 on launch day. It matched or edged out Fable 5 in our testing at a lower cost per task.
pull_quote.role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Cognition

data_points.label: Cache read price cut, to $0.25/M tokens
Fewer cyber safeguard interventions per session
Base input/output price per million, unchanged

stories.article_excerpt: Anthropic shipped a frontier model on Monday, and the two things that will actually change how enterprises use it are both footnotes.

stories.headline: Perplexity Wants Your Mac to Do the Private Half of the Work
stories.key_takeaway: Perplexity's hybrid compute splits a single agent task between cloud frontier models and a local model on the user's Apple silicon Mac, using an open-sourced 0.6B on-device PII classifier as the gate - a privacy pitch that also shifts inference cost onto hardware the customer already owns.

pull_quote.text: Mac offers a big opportunity to move token consumption to Apple Silicon (with no price paid for tokens consumed locally) and protect user privacy.

stories.article_excerpt: For three years, the AI industry's answer to can I trust you with my tax returns has been to build a higher wall around the cloud.

stories.headline: Google and Alibaba Both Shipped a Flagship on September 2. Neither Mentioned the Other.
stories.key_takeaway: Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash and Alibaba's Qwen3.8-Max-0902 landed inside the same UTC day without acknowledging each other, and the pricing that actually separates them is cache reads and license terms, not the sticker gap most trackers advertise.

pull_quote.text: Gemini 3.8 Flash delivers substantial gains from 3.7 Flash, often approaching the performance of higher-cost frontier models.
pull_quote.role: Senior Director of Product Management, Google

data_points.label: Gemini 3.8 Flash Intelligence Index, up 3 points
Gemini 3.8 Flash pricing per million, through Dec 31

stories.article_excerpt: Inside a single UTC day, the two labs with the fastest shipping cadence in the industry each pushed a new flagship into production.

stories.headline: The Same Question, a Different Nationality, a Different Safety Warning
stories.key_takeaway: Google's AI Overviews routed near-identical queries into emergency safety warnings or friendly small talk depending on the nationality named, exposing bias that surfaced through safety-classifier routing rather than generated text - at a scale of 2.5 billion monthly users.

pull_quote.text: We agree that the results for these types of searches aren't what they should be, and we're working on improvements. Results can vary a lot from search to search.

data_points.label: Chatbots showing the pattern in extended tests
From acknowledgment to prompts no longer reproducing

stories.article_excerpt: Type a short sentence into Google and, for most of the past two weeks, the AI Overview at the top of the results changed with one word.

stories.headline: OpenAI's Astra Found Two Chrome Zero-Days Nobody Asked It to Look For
stories.key_takeaway: Astra is the first model OpenAI has ever rated Critical under its Preparedness Framework, and the company is using tiered access rather than regulation to decide who gets the capability - on numbers no outside party has verified.

pull_quote.text: A capable model does not operate inside a framework document. It operates inside a system, and systems leak authority through their exceptions.

data_points.label: Cyber jailbreak refusal rate, up from 59%
High-severity flaws in the internal benchmark

stories.article_excerpt: The exam was supposed to be a closed book. OpenAI had assembled 20 high-severity vulnerabilities in Chrome's V8 engine.

stories.headline: The EU Just Called ChatGPT a Search Engine. That Word Carries a 6% Penalty.
stories.key_takeaway: By designating ChatGPT a Very Large Online Search Engine on a capability test rather than a product category, the Commission showed it can regulate generative AI through the platform law it already has - and built a template that applies to Gemini, Claude and Perplexity the moment they cross 45 million EU users.

pull_quote.text: We continue to watch the digital landscape closely and will not hesitate to designate any platform that meets the threshold for enhanced supervision under the Digital Services Act.

stories.article_excerpt: The European Commission did not pass a new law. It did not wait for one either.

stories.headline: Police Called It a Medical Episode. Tesla's Federal Filing Says the Driver-Assist Was On.
stories.key_takeaway: Tesla's federal crash filing shows its driver-assist was verified engaged at 104 mph in a fatal Clute, Texas crash that police publicly attributed to a medical episode, but the company redacted the narrative and software version, leaving even regulators unable to tell what the car actually did.

pull_quote.text: The public was told this was likely a medical episode. Tesla's own records say its automation was verified engaged in the crash. Both can't be the whole story.

data_points.label: Pre-crash speed logged on a residential street
Tesla crash reports with narrative redacted
Tesla Level 2 crashes reported to NHTSA
Concurrent open NHTSA investigations into FSD

stories.article_excerpt: On the afternoon of May 20, 2026, a Tesla Model 3 left Brazoswood Drive in Clute, Texas, and went through a fence.

stories.headline: The Autonomous Coding Agent Ran Code It Was Never Supposed to Run
stories.key_takeaway: Johann Rehberger showed that a classifier-backed auto-approval mode can be steered into executing attacker-supplied code most of the time through a chain of individually benign steps, making sandboxing and egress control, not permission prompts, the real defence.

pull_quote.text: Ironically, that safety decision is the exploit path.

data_points.label: Attack success rate across three variants
Injection rate in the vendor-commissioned evaluation
Share of permission prompts users approve anyway

stories.article_excerpt: The prompt was three words and a URL: summarize this website. No jailbreak phrasing, none of the crude override attempts.

stories.headline: Everyone Benchmarks What Agents Can Do. Almost Nobody Benchmarks What They Cost.
stories.key_takeaway: An ACL 2026 survey of agent evaluation finds that cost-efficiency, safety and robustness remain largely unmeasured, and independent audits show agents separated by two accuracy points can differ ninefold in price.

pull_quote.text: Cost-blind leaderboards now mislead by design, because they reward extra spending without reporting what that spending bought.

data_points.label: Cost gap between agents two points apart
Per-task cost spread on SWE-bench Verified
Benchmarks where the priciest model hit the frontier

stories.article_excerpt: Two web agents ran the same benchmark. One scored 40% and burned $1,577 in API fees. The other scored 42% and cost $171.
